title: Ex-Google Recruiter: Why The Best Candidate Doesn't Get The Job
description:
Get my Job Seekers Toolkit: https://stan.store/farahsharghi/p/get-my-job-seekers-toolkit-now
 Book a 1:1: https://stan.store/farahsharghi/p/book-a-1hour-career-coaching-session-with-me-eq3bs

You're not getting hired because somewhere along the way, every time you tried to be likeable in the interview, every time you over-explained why you'd be "such a great fit," you weren't aligning to what the hiring team needed.

I spent over a decade recruiting at Google, TikTok, Uber, Lyft, and The New York Times. I've watched qualified people get passed over because they walked in trying to be chosen instead of trying to be aligned. Same skills. Same experience. Completely different outcome.

In this video, I'm telling you exactly what's happening on the other side of the table when you're in 'pick me' mode, why being 'liked' has nothing to do with getting hired, and the one word that needs to replace "pick me, choose me, love me" if you actually want offers to start landing for jobs you want.

The candidates getting hired right now aren't the ones who want it the most. They're the ones who stopped auditioning.
